status_note: implementation_status is measured against each full end-to-end global requirement. Feature 001 foundation code and tests are implemented, but no global requirement is considered fully complete until its owning feature meets all listed acceptance criteria. Current foundation evidence is recorded in docs/traceability/traceability.md; remote GitHub Actions execution is unverified because this workspace has no Git remote.

priority_legend.P0: Non-negotiable safety, privacy, integrity, or architecture constraint.
priority_legend.P1: Required product or assessment acceptance criterion.
priority_legend.P2: Expected quality requirement unless an approved ADR records an exception.
priority_legend.P3: Optional improvement; not a release blocker without an approved scope change.

unresolved_question_register.question: Which challenge-provided or approved public corpus, policy theme, licence, and usage rights should Feature 002 use?
unresolved_question_register.reason: No separate challenge brief, dataset, or source registry was present in the inspected workspace. Do not acquire or invent sources before this is resolved.

unresolved_question_register.question: Is any production deployment target required beyond local assessment use?
unresolved_question_register.reason: Feature 001 assumes local development only; hosting, authentication, network exposure, and operations would materially change if production deployment is required.

unresolved_question_register.question: Which Apple-silicon host and pinned MLX model will be available for local-provider verification?
unresolved_question_register.reason: The current host is Linux x86_64 and cannot provide Apple-silicon MLX runtime evidence.

unresolved_question_register.question: Should the supplied POLICYLENS_MASTER_SPEC.md be renamed or copied to the master specification's suggested MASTER_SPEC_PROMPT.md path?
unresolved_question_register.reason: The supplied filename differs from the canonical path named inside the specification; the supplied source was preserved unchanged in this run.

requirements.description: Use the canonical PolicyLens identity, tagline, repository, package, service, collection, API, and MCP server names unless an approved ADR changes them.
acceptance_criteria: Names in user-facing and deployable artifacts match the canonical identity table.
No alternative product name is introduced.

requirements.description: Serve policy researchers, analysts, reviewers, ML engineers, and governance/security reviewers with evidence they can inspect.
acceptance_criteria: A user can ask a corpus-scoped question and inspect the source passages or structured rows supporting the response.
The product states that it is not a final authority for consequential decisions.

requirements.description: Answer only from retrieved evidence or deterministic tool output, and clarify, abstain, or expose conflicts when support is inadequate.
acceptance_criteria: Every corpus-derived factual claim has valid supporting evidence.
Insufficient, ambiguous, conflicting, unavailable, or out-of-scope requests use the corresponding safe outcome.
expected_evidence: Claim-level citation and abstention evaluation cases

requirements.description: Keep the system local-first, evidence-grounded, bounded, and limited to three deployable services; exclude autonomous consequential actions and unrestricted browsing.
acceptance_criteria: The deployable system has only frontend, backend/agent host, and MCP services unless an ADR approves an exception.
No unrestricted browsing or consequential write action is exposed.

requirements.description: Build the frontend with React 18+, TypeScript, and Vite; keep it accessible, responsive to 320 CSS pixels, and keyboard/screen-reader usable.
requirements.source_section: Sections 4.1 A, Frontend implementation contract, 20 Feature 009
acceptance_criteria: Semantic controls have labels and visible focus.
Layout remains usable at 320 CSS pixels and contrast meets the selected accessibility standard.
expected_evidence: Responsive browser tests and accessibility audit

requirements.description: Provide a research workspace with query, optional filters, permitted provider selection, submit/cancel, progressive status, and in-memory recent runs.
requirements.source_section: Section 4.1 A and Frontend implementation contract
acceptance_criteria: A user can submit a valid query and see progress without hidden reasoning.
Cancellation and validation/unavailable states are visible where supported.
expected_evidence: Playwright happy-path, cancellation, and failure-path tests

requirements.description: Separate answer claims, passage citations, source metadata, calculations, uncertainty, conflicts, limitations, and bounded evidence details.
acceptance_criteria: Each displayed claim can be traced to a citation or deterministic result.
Evidence detail shows exact bounded text or rows and provenance; untrusted content is rendered as text, not HTML.

requirements.description: Expose provider/model mode, trace ID, safe tool-activity summaries, copy actions, and explicit approval before any consequential action.
acceptance_criteria: Run metadata is visible without private reasoning or sensitive tool arguments.
No consequential action can proceed without explicit user approval.
expected_evidence: Component tests for provider, trace, tool, copy, and approval states

requirements.description: Consume a versioned backend contract and provide status and clear loading, empty, partial, timeout, offline, validation, permission, and server-error states.
acceptance_criteria: Browser calls only the backend and receives no provider key or direct corpus/index access.
Streaming, if enabled, uses typed accepted/retrieving/tool/validation/completion/failure/cancel events with progress summaries only.
expected_evidence: Network boundary tests and browser-level state tests

requirements.description: Provide component tests and browser-level happy, abstention, and failed-tool paths.
requirements.source_section: Section 4.1 A and Frontend implementation contract
acceptance_criteria: CI executes frontend unit tests and at least the required browser-level workflows before the frontend feature is complete.

requirements.description: Use Python 3.12+, FastAPI, and Pydantic for typed, versioned API contracts, request validation, run state, safe errors, and health reporting.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid request shapes fail with stable machine-readable errors.
Liveness/readiness responses disclose no secret or internal infrastructure detail.

requirements.description: Keep the backend as the sole host for retrieval orchestration, the bounded agent runtime, MCP client lifecycle, provider routing, guardrails, and citation validation.
acceptance_criteria: Frontend and MCP service do not own backend Chroma access or model-provider credentials.
Agent execution follows explicit states and runtime budgets.

requirements.description: Validate structured model output, citation provenance, policy outcomes, and error mapping before returning an answer.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown or unretrieved citation IDs are rejected.
Answer status invariants are enforced before response serialization.

requirements.description: Generate correlated traces and redacted structured logs, with documented authentication boundary and stable error taxonomy.
acceptance_criteria: Every run has a trace/correlation ID and safe terminal status.
Sensitive query/evidence/credential values are absent from default logs and traces.

requirements.description: Implement a reproducible query path from input validation through filtered BM25+dense retrieval, fusion, context selection, grounded generation, citation checks, and uncertainty reporting.
acceptance_criteria: A run records its corpus/index version and retrieved evidence IDs.
Retrieval failure is distinguishable from generation failure and no-result is explicit.

requirements.description: Apply metadata and permission filters, deterministic deduplication/context ordering, bounded token selection, and explicit untrusted-evidence delimiters; evaluate any query rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: Unauthorized evidence is never returned to generation or users.
Rewriting is disabled unless evaluation demonstrates it preserves entities, dates, qualifiers, and negation.

requirements.description: Retain a simple non-agent RAG baseline and compare it with the bounded agent only on cases that require tools or multi-step evidence work.
acceptance_criteria: The baseline and agent use the same frozen cases and comparable generation settings.
Any agent complexity has measured benefit or is removed.

requirements.description: Use at least one structured and one unstructured source; all sources must be public, synthetic, or appropriately anonymized and have lawful, documented usage rights.
acceptance_criteria: The corpus manifest identifies type, provenance, licence, date, checksum, sensitivity, and allowed use for every source.
At least two reproducible EDA findings use actual acquired data and state caveats.
expected_evidence: Validated corpus manifest and source snapshots

requirements.description: Maintain an allow-listed, versioned source registry and immutable raw snapshots with checksums, media type, parser, refresh policy, and allowed usage.
acceptance_criteria: Changed source hashes create a new corpus version instead of silently replacing raw data.
Downloads use explicit host/path allow-lists, size limits, timeouts, bounded retries, and MIME checks.

requirements.description: Make acquisition and every derived-data stage idempotent and emit machine-readable run manifests with inputs, outputs, versions, parameters, timing, warnings, and rejects.
acceptance_criteria: Derived outputs can be rebuilt from retained raw snapshots and configuration.
Repeated runs over unchanged inputs preserve deterministic IDs and hashes.

requirements.description: Normalize parsed reports into a canonical document representation that preserves pages, blocks, section paths, offsets, provenance, and parser version.
acceptance_criteria: Each parsed artifact validates against a versioned canonical schema.
Stable source/document identity and content checksum are retained.

requirements.description: Preserve structured-data columns, types, units, dimensions, row keys, missing-value semantics, and dictionaries; record OCR/parsing limitations and quality issues.
acceptance_criteria: Structured calculations use exact typed rows rather than lossy prose flattening.
Missing values, duplicates, OCR uncertainty, exclusions, and known quality issues are documented.

requirements.description: Implement versioned structure-aware chunking that preserves headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, footnotes, page/offset locations, and bounded same-section overlap.
acceptance_criteria: Chunks respect configured token bounds without merging documents or silently truncating embedded inputs.
Verbatim evidence is stored separately from any context-prefixed embedding text.

requirements.description: Generate deterministic stable chunk IDs and compare fixed-size, structure-aware, and one alternative chunk size on the frozen retrieval set.
acceptance_criteria: Identical immutable input and configuration reproduce chunk text and IDs.
Chunk strategy selection reports retrieval, citation, index-size, ingestion-time, and latency evidence.

requirements.description: Provide coexisting local-default and OpenAI embedding implementations behind a provider-neutral interface; select them independently from generation through EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=local|openai, with pinned model revision and recorded dimensions, limits, pooling, normalization, licence, and hash where available.
acceptance_criteria: Document and query vectors use compatible model semantics.
Both local and OpenAI providers remain available; one is selected explicitly per run without silently replacing the other or falling back.
A model change creates a distinct version and requires a full re-index.

requirements.description: Use bounded batching and content-addressed caching; reject dimension mismatch and over-limit input rather than mixing vectors or silently truncating.
acceptance_criteria: Cache key includes embedding version and content hash.
Invalid dimensions, non-finite vectors, and oversized inputs fail with stable errors.
expected_evidence: Embedding cache, boundary, and dimension tests

requirements.description: Use backend-owned local persistent Chroma with deterministic, versioned collections, pinned distance metric, complete provenance metadata, and permission/source filters.
acceptance_criteria: Collection names encode corpus, embedding, and schema versions.
The frontend and MCP service cannot access Chroma directly.

requirements.description: Validate a new index before atomically activating it; retain rollback metadata and fail closed on incompatible schema, dimensions, embedder, or corpus version.
acceptance_criteria: Partial failure never changes the active index.
Persistence survives restart and an incompatible collection is rejected.

requirements.description: Treat generated indexes as rebuildable derived data and exclude them, model weights, restricted raw data, and secret-bearing traces from Git.
acceptance_criteria: Ignore rules cover configured index and secret paths.
A clean index can be rebuilt from retained, permitted source snapshots and manifests.

requirements.description: Build a local BM25 index over the same stable passage IDs and record tokenizer, stopword, stemming, field, and version configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Keyword results resolve to canonical passage IDs and preserve permission metadata.
Index configuration and version are reproducible.

requirements.description: Fuse keyword and dense results deterministically with documented rank fusion, deduplicate overlaps, cap source dominance, clamp top-k, and record scores/ranks.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated queries with identical indexes/configuration produce identical fused ordering.
Permission and source filters are applied before evidence is returned.

requirements.description: Compare BM25, dense, and hybrid retrieval, plus one meaningful chunking or filter variable, on a frozen set using the same relevant evidence labels.
acceptance_criteria: Recall@k and MRR are reported overall and by case type; graded relevance adds nDCG@k.
Latency and empty-result rates are retained alongside quality metrics.
expected_evidence: Experiment registry entries and evaluation report

requirements.description: Attach citations to individual claims with stable source/passage IDs, title, page/section or row keys, bounded quote, URI where available, and audit metadata.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewer can open each citation and verify the exact supporting passage or structured rows.
Calculations include tool and input-row provenance.

requirements.description: Reject unknown or unreturned evidence IDs and enforce status-specific response invariants for answered, clarify, abstain, conflict, blocked, and failed-safe outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: An answered corpus claim has valid citations; a conflict presents both sides; an abstention gives an evidence-based reason.
No model-generated citation is accepted solely because it is well-formed.

requirements.description: Use the OpenAI Agents SDK in the backend for a bounded single-agent workflow only where tool/evidence selection adds measured value; keep a non-agent baseline.
acceptance_criteria: SDK version and supported model/tool/structured-output behavior are verified and pinned before implementation.
No multi-agent architecture is added without measured benefit and an ADR.

requirements.description: Represent agent execution as finite explicit states with bounded turns, calls, retries, timeouts, tokens, context, and response size.
acceptance_criteria: Every transition has validated inputs, trace event, bounded attempts, and safe failure transition.
Budget exhaustion terminates safely and returns a trace ID.

requirements.description: Use deterministic typed tools, correct only transient failures with bounded retries, and stop safely on invalid arguments or malformed output.
acceptance_criteria: Arithmetic, filtering, citation construction, and policy checks do not rely on model arithmetic.
Invalid arguments are not blindly retried and unsafe provider fallback is prohibited.

requirements.description: Run an independent MCP server with at least one useful deterministic read-only tool and one provenance-bearing passage resource; document host/client/server roles.
acceptance_criteria: A host can discover and invoke the approved tool and resolve the resource URI.
The resource identifies its content as untrusted and includes source, location, checksum, sensitivity, and licence.

requirements.description: Validate tool inputs/outputs, server identity, capabilities, schema versions, identifier bounds, timeouts, cancellation, and stable error codes at both host and server.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown server identity/capability or malformed output fails closed.
Path traversal, oversized requests, excessive rows, unsupported operations, and non-finite values are rejected.
expected_evidence: MCP contract and adversarial input tests

requirements.description: Keep MCP read-only by default, prohibit arbitrary shell/SQL/filesystem/URL/code tools, and compare MCP with a thin direct-call baseline in an ADR or experiment.
acceptance_criteria: Only explicitly named, typed capabilities are exposed.
The comparison records interoperability, lifecycle, latency, operational overhead, debugging, trust, and authorization tradeoffs.
expected_evidence: Approved MCP/direct integration ADR and comparison

requirements.description: Provide a configuration-driven OpenAI API route as the initial generation path behind the common model interface, while retaining the local MLX route as an additive option; pin actual model IDs during planning and protect secrets and sensitive inputs.
acceptance_criteria: OpenAI is selected for the first API-based generation setup; provider, model, prompt version, usage, and fallback decision are recorded.
Missing credentials fail safely; live-provider tests are opt-in and mocks are the default.
Selecting OpenAI generation does not override the independently selected embedding provider.
expected_evidence: Opt-in live compatibility evidence with redacted traces

requirements.description: Retain an additive, configuration-driven local Apple-silicon MLX/MLX-LM adapter path through the common model interface, loopback by default, with bounded context/output and explicit capability reporting; runtime verification is deferred to an Apple-silicon host.
acceptance_criteria: The local route reports health, model metadata, supported capabilities, limits, and quantization/memory notes.
Local mode works without an OpenAI key when local generation and embeddings are selected.
expected_evidence: Local model metadata and resource report

requirements.description: Never assume native MLX tool calling or silent degradation; use a validated constrained adapter if needed, and never send local/private requests to OpenAI without user approval.
acceptance_criteria: Unsupported model capabilities are surfaced rather than silently emulated.
Provider fallback is explicit, observable, and consent-gated.

requirements.description: Compare OpenAI and MLX on the same frozen subset for tool reliability, structured validity, groundedness, answer quality, latency, memory, and cost where measurable.
acceptance_criteria: Provider parity is not claimed without comparable measurements and platform notes.
Unmeasurable local memory or throughput values are marked unavailable, not invented.
expected_evidence: Provider comparison experiment and limitations section

requirements.description: Document assets, identities, data classifications, controls, failure behavior, and abuse cases across all nine specified trust boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Threat model covers browser, API, providers, MCP, corpus, evaluators, and logs/traces.
Residual risks are explicit; prompt injection is not described as solved.

requirements.description: Treat user, retrieved, model, MCP, and tool content as untrusted; enforce delimiters, input/output schemas, permission filters, tool allow-lists, and citation post-validation.
acceptance_criteria: Instruction injection in each untrusted source does not override system policy or trigger an unauthorized tool.
Unauthorized evidence and forged citations are rejected.

requirements.description: Use least privilege, explicit server allow-lists, bounded payloads/rates/retries/timeouts, cancellation, redaction, and user approval for consequential actions.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown server identity and excessive requests fail closed.
No consequential action proceeds without explicit approval and audited outcome.
expected_evidence: MCP identity, resource-bound, timeout, and rate tests

requirements.description: Keep secrets outside source control and browser configuration; redact credentials, personal data, sensitive parameters, document bodies, and private traces.
acceptance_criteria: `.env.example` contains placeholders only and VITE variables contain no secrets.
Tests demonstrate secrets and protected content do not appear in default logs/traces.

requirements.description: Use only public, synthetic, or suitably anonymized sources and apply data minimization, permission-aware retrieval, retention, and access controls.
acceptance_criteria: Every source has sensitivity, licence, and usage metadata.
Restricted or unauthorized evidence cannot enter answers, logs, or evaluations.

requirements.description: Require human oversight for consequential uses and explicit user consent before private/local inputs are sent to an external provider.
acceptance_criteria: The UI and documentation state intended-use limits.
Provider changes that alter data handling require explicit user approval.

requirements.description: Record correlated run/trace IDs, provider/model, prompt/index versions, retrieval IDs/scores, MCP server/tool status, transitions, retries, validation, latency, usage, cost, and terminal status without private reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: Run events support audit and failure diagnosis without hidden chain-of-thought.
Sensitive content is redacted according to documented policy.

requirements.description: Maintain an experiment registry and machine-readable pipeline/run manifests containing code, environment, lock, corpus, index, prompt, model, seed, parameters, metrics, and artifact references.
acceptance_criteria: Every reported result resolves to a complete reproducibility record.
Missing values or unavailable measurements are explicit.

requirements.description: Freeze and review at least 30 representative cases with separate labels/evidence, leakage controls, case categories, lineage, and dev/test split.
acceptance_criteria: The set covers factual, synthesis, calculation, ambiguity, abstention, conflict, injection, MCP failures, sensitive requests, and local-model failures.
No final test labels are embedded in runtime prompts or used directly for tuning.
expected_evidence: Reviewed evaluation manifest with at least 30 cases

requirements.description: Compare keyword, dense, hybrid, agent/non-agent, OpenAI/MLX, and at least one chunking or filter alternative while changing one principal variable at a time where practical.
acceptance_criteria: Each comparison uses a recorded configuration, same frozen subset, and justified baseline.
Negative results are retained.

requirements.description: Report retrieval, answer, citation, abstention, conflict, structured-output, tool, injection, latency, token, cost, and measurable local-resource metrics by case type where feasible.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics include uncertainty/limitations appropriate to sample size.
No threshold is invented before a baseline is measured.
expected_evidence: Evaluation report with metric definitions and reproducible outputs
Bootstrap intervals where the sample supports them

requirements.description: Use deterministic evaluators where possible; calibrate any LLM judge against human review and perform documented human review across case categories.
acceptance_criteria: Judge model/rubric, blinding, disagreement, and known bias are reported.
Failed cases include expected/observed behavior, layer, root-cause hypothesis, severity, intervention, and regression test.

requirements.description: Test acquisition, parsing, chunking, embedding, indexing, retrieval, deterministic tools, schemas, citations, state transitions, routing, and redaction at unit level.
acceptance_criteria: Each implemented boundary and deterministic operation has focused automated tests.
Each test identifies the requirement IDs it verifies.
expected_evidence: Unit-test suite and requirement tags/traceability check

requirements.description: Exercise frontend/API, backend/model, backend/MCP, tool/resource schema, index lifecycle, and end-to-end agent/tool/citation contracts and failures.
acceptance_criteria: Mocks are default for external providers; live tests are opt-in.
Timeout, cancellation, malformed response, unavailable service, restart persistence, and safe recovery paths are tested.

requirements.description: Run adversarial security tests and deterministic smoke evaluation in CI; reserve full offline evaluation for on-demand or release and prevent quality/safety regressions.
acceptance_criteria: CI checks injection, permissions, secret redaction, schema/citation validity, and tool boundaries.
Promotion gates cover safety and quality and are set only after baseline measurement.
expected_evidence: Security smoke and offline evaluation reports

requirements.description: Pin Python dependencies with uv and frontend dependencies with a committed npm lockfile; record selected runtime and Spec Kit versions.
acceptance_criteria: A clean environment can install exactly the committed lock state.
External SDK behavior is verified against the pinned package version.

requirements.description: Version source manifests, raw snapshot hashes, canonical data, chunker/embedder parameters, index versions, prompt hashes, model IDs, and experiment settings.
acceptance_criteria: Every derived artifact identifies its exact inputs and configuration.
Index changes are rebuildable and cannot silently mutate provenance.
expected_evidence: Manifest completeness and deterministic rebuild tests

requirements.description: Maintain a PolicyLens README with problem, setup, run commands, data acquisition, sample queries, architecture, evaluation, limitations, and responsible-use notes.
acceptance_criteria: A clean-checkout setup and local service execution path is documented and verified.
Limitations and unsupported behavior are prominent.
expected_evidence: README setup walkthrough from a clean environment

requirements.description: Produce architecture and trust-boundary diagrams, data sheet, evaluation report, model/system card, threat model, limitations, innovation assessment, and demo runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Each deliverable matches observable implementation and cites reproducible evidence where it makes quality claims.
All nine trust boundaries and ten demo scenarios are represented.

requirements.description: Maintain ADRs, stable requirement IDs, a generated traceability matrix, and exact scenario mappings for every requirement and required demo.
acceptance_criteria: Every requirement and acceptance criterion maps to implementation or planned tests/evaluation/inspection evidence.
Unmapped requirements and tasks are detectable before implementation.
expected_evidence: ADR index and scenario mapping review

requirements.description: Keep frontend, backend, and MCP independently runnable with documented local endpoints and common development/test commands.
acceptance_criteria: Each service starts and can be health-checked independently from a clean environment.
Documented ports are frontend 5173, backend 8000, API docs 8000/docs, and local MLX endpoint 127.0.0.1:8080/v1 when used.

requirements.description: Keep browser configuration non-secret, Chroma/BM25 local and backend-owned, MLX loopback by default, and generated data/indexes out of source control.
acceptance_criteria: Local mode starts without an OpenAI key when local providers are selected.
Configured paths are ignored and no client-side code accesses data stores or model endpoints directly.

requirements.description: Validate the `.env.example` contract with typed settings, safe defaults, incompatible-combination errors, and explicit provider/MCP timeout and runtime budgets.
acceptance_criteria: No real credentials appear in the example file.
Provider values are canonicalized consistently; the plan resolves the source's `local` versus `mlx` spelling conflict to `openai|mlx`.
expected_evidence: Secret scan and configuration contract review
